definition_en: a list of names, addresses or files arranged so that a particular item can be found
core_image: 前台抽屉里一本厚册子，一列列名字和号码排得像梯子
scene: 册子摊在台面上，纸边被翻得起了毛。He found the number in the telephone directory.
sceneCN: 这里 directory 指「名录」（第 1 个义项：按顺序排列的名单册）；句意是他在电话簿里查到了那个号码。

senses.title: A book of names and numbers
senses.definition: a book or list that gives names, addresses or telephone numbers in order
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序列出姓名、地址或电话的册子或清单
senses.example: He found the number in the telephone directory.
senses.exampleCN: 他在电话簿里查到了那个号码。
senses.why: A town full of strangers becomes findable once the names are set in rows.
senses.whyCN: 一城陌生人，只要名字排成行，就变得可以找到了。

senses.title: An index of stored items
senses.definition: a list that shows where things are kept or how they are arranged
senses.definitionCN: 标明东西存放位置或排列方式的清单
senses.example: The directory at the back of the report lists every table.
senses.exampleCN: 报告末尾的目录列出了每一张表。
senses.why: The list does not hold the thing, only the way to reach it.
senses.whyCN: 这份清单不装着东西，只装着找到东西的路。

senses.title: A folder on a computer
senses.definition: a named area on a computer that holds files and other folders
senses.definitionCN: 电脑里存放文件与其他文件夹的有名空间
senses.example: Save the pictures in a separate directory.
senses.exampleCN: 把这些图片存到另一个文件夹里。
senses.why: The paper list became a room, and the room can hold rooms inside it.
senses.whyCN: 纸上的清单变成了一间屋子，而屋子还能再装屋子。

intro.en: Directory began as a medieval Latin directorium, a guide or book of rules, and only later became a list of names.
intro.cn: directory 原是中世纪拉丁语 directorium，指指南或规则手册，后来才变成名单。

items.en: Dirigere meant to set straight and to guide a course.
items.cn: dirigere 指拉直，也指引导方向。

items.en: Directorium named a guide or a book that told people what to do.
items.cn: directorium 指指南，或告诉人该怎么做的书。

items.en: English directory first meant a set of directions or rules.
items.cn: 英语里的 directory 最初指一套指示或规则。

items.en: The word shifted to a book of names, addresses and numbers.
items.cn: 这个词转而指收录姓名、地址与号码的册子。

items.en: Computing added the sense of a folder that lists files.
items.cn: 计算机又给它添了「列出文件的文件夹」这一义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the direct- stem, while the meaning group names other ordered lists.
note.cn: 形近组共用 direct 这一段词干，近义组则列出其他有序的清单。

entries.definition: to guide a course or to aim something straight
entries.definitionCN: 指引方向或把某物对准

entries.definition: the line along which someone or something moves
entries.definitionCN: 人或物移动所沿的路线

entries.definition: a person who controls how a film is made
entries.definitionCN: 掌管电影拍摄的人

entries.definition: an ordered list that points to where information is found
entries.definitionCN: 指向信息所在位置的有序清单

entries.definition: a list of goods or items arranged for reference
entries.definitionCN: 供查阅而编排的货品或条目清单

entries.definition: a published list of names, events or properties
entries.definitionCN: 公布出来的名单、活动或房产清单

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from a thick book of names to a folder that holds other folders.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一本厚厚的名单册，走到能装下其他文件夹的文件夹。

normal.en: Direct plus -ory is a place where things are set in order.
normal.cn: direct 加 -ory，就是把东西排整齐的地方。

normal.en: A telephone directory turns a city into rows of names.
normal.cn: 电话簿把一座城变成一排排名字。

normal.en: A directory never holds the thing, only its address.
normal.cn: 名录从不装着东西，只装着它的地址。

normal.en: On a computer, a directory is a folder with a name.
normal.cn: 在电脑里，directory 就是有名字的文件夹。

normal.en: Look up the name, then follow the number.
normal.cn: 先查名字，再顺着号码找过去。

abstract.en: Picture a finger sliding down a column of names.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指沿着一列名字往下滑。

abstract.en: Picture a page thin enough to show the print from behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一页薄纸，背面的字都透了过来。

abstract.en: Picture a folder opening to show smaller folders inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个文件夹打开，里面还有更小的文件夹。

examples.en: The library keeps a directory of local clubs.
examples.cn: 图书馆存着一份本地社团名录。

examples.en: She searched the directory for his office number.
examples.cn: 她在名录里查他办公室的号码。

examples.en: Copy the file into the main directory.
examples.cn: 把这个文件复制到主文件夹里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 directory 记成「的名字全录」：direct 是排直，-ory 是地方，把名字排直放好的地方就是名录。

root: 来自拉丁语 dirigere（拉直、指引）的名词形式 directorium，本指指南或规则手册。英语先用它表示指示与规则，十八世纪后转向姓名地址录，计算机时代又用来指存放文件的文件夹。

sensesIntro.en: From a printed book of names, to an index of stored things, to a folder on a screen.
sensesIntro.cn: 从印着名字的册子，到存放物品的索引，再到屏幕上的文件夹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick book of names set in straight rows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本厚册子，名字排成笔直的行。

chain: THE NAMES ARE COPIED IN ORDER
A COMPUTER KEEPS ITS OWN LIST
FILES SIT INSIDE A NAMED SPACE

branches.en: The first sense is the printed book of names and numbers.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是那本印着姓名与号码的册子。

branches.en: The second sense narrows the book to a guide of places.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这本书收窄成指路的清单。

branches.en: The third sense gives the list a room inside a machine.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把这份清单搬进机器里的一间屋子。

branches.en: A book and an index both answer one question: where is it.
branches.cn: 册子和索引都在回答同一个问题：它在哪儿。

branches.en: Both arrange hidden things so that one search finds them.
branches.cn: 两者都把藏着的东西排好，让一次查找就能找到。

intro.en: Directory belongs to the direct- family, words about straight lines and guidance.
intro.cn: directory 属于 direct 一族词，围绕直线与指引。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base dirigere, to set straight, yields direct-, seen in direct, direction and directory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 dirigere（拉直）给出 direct，见于 direct、direction 与 directory。

items.meaning: a place or book that keeps things in order
items.example: The directory lists every member of the club.
items.exampleCN: 这份名录列出了俱乐部的每位成员。

items.example: He directed us to the nearest station.
items.exampleCN: 他给我们指了最近的车站。

items.meaning: the line along which something moves
items.example: She walked in the direction of the river.
The director smiled at the finished scene.
items.exampleCN: 导演看着拍完的这场戏笑了。

items.example: The directive was short and firm.

items.meaning: in a straight line or with nothing between
items.example: The road runs directly to the coast.

items.meaning: not straight or not stated openly
items.example: Her reply was polite but indirect.

items.meaning: to send or aim something wrongly
items.example: A wrong label misdirected the parcel.
items.exampleCN: 一个错误的标签把包裹送错了地方。

definition_zh: n. 残疾；伤残；障碍；（法律）无行为能力
definition_en: a physical or mental condition that limits movements, senses or activities; also a legal disqualification
core_image: 轮椅前的一段平缓坡道和一颗大大的自动门按钮；表格上「是否有残疾」那一栏
scene: 她从不把残疾当成障碍。She never treats her disability as a barrier.
sceneCN: 这里 disability 是「残疾」（第 1 个义项：限制日常活动的身体或心智状况）；句意是她从不把残疾当成障碍。图中可辨识物件：轮椅、平缓的坡道、自动门按钮。

pos.zh: 残疾；伤残；障碍；（法律）无行为能力

senses.title: A limiting condition
senses.definition: a physical or mental condition that limits movements, senses or activities
senses.definitionCN: （名词）限制行动、感官或活动的身体或心智状况
senses.example: She never treats her disability as a barrier.
senses.exampleCN: 她从不把残疾当成障碍。
senses.why: A wheelchair at the foot of a smooth ramp beside a wide door button.
senses.whyCN: 轮椅停在平缓坡道下，旁边是一个宽大的开门按钮。

senses.title: Plain lack of capacity
senses.definition: the state of being unable to do something
senses.definitionCN: （名词）做不到某事的状态
senses.example: The injury left him with a temporary disability.
senses.exampleCN: 那次受伤让他暂时丧失了能力。
senses.why: A hand in a sling resting beside an unopened toolbox.
senses.whyCN: 一只吊着绷带的手放在没打开的工具箱旁。

senses.title: A legal bar
senses.definition: a legal disqualification from acting, such as signing a contract
senses.definitionCN: （名词）法律上被剥夺行动资格，如签合同
senses.example: The contract ended because of legal disability.
senses.exampleCN: 合同因法律上的无行为能力而终止。
senses.why: A contract with the signature line left blank and a stamp beside it.
senses.whyCN: 一份合同的签名栏空着，旁边放着印章。

intro.en: Disability is dis- not plus ability, which comes through Old French able from Latin habilis, handy, from habere, to have or hold.
intro.cn: disability 是 dis-（不）加 ability；ability 经古法语 able 来自拉丁语 habilis（顺手的），habilis 又来自 habere（拥有、握住）。

items.en: Habere meant to have or hold.
items.cn: habere 意为拥有、握住。

items.en: Habilis meant handy or fit.
items.cn: habilis 意为顺手的、合适的。

items.en: Old French able meant capable.
items.cn: 古法语 able 意为有能力的。

items.en: Ability entered English for capacity.
items.cn: 十五世纪 ability 以「能力」义进入英语。

items.en: Dis- turned it into lack of capacity.
items.cn: 十六世纪 dis- 把它变成能力的缺失。

items.en: The word became central to access and rights.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个词成为无障碍与权利议题的核心。

note.en: The look-alike group is the ability family; the near-meaning group names medical and legal terms for lost function.
note.cn: 形近组是 ability 家族；近义组是表示功能丧失的医学与法律用词。

entries.definition: The power or skill to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的力量或技能。

entries.definition: Having a disability, or switched off.
entries.definitionCN: 有残疾的，或被停用的。

entries.definition: Simply not being able to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 单纯地做不到某事。

entries.definition: A loss or weakening of a body function.
entries.definitionCN: 某项身体功能的丧失或减弱。

entries.definition: An older word for a disabling condition, now often avoided.
entries.definitionCN: 表示致残状况的旧词，如今常被回避。

entries.definition: A legal inability to act or decide.
entries.definitionCN: 法律上不能行动或决定。

normalIntro.en: Disability is dis- not plus ability: the capacity to hold or do has been taken away.
normalIntro.cn: disability 就是 dis-（不）加 ability：握住或去做的那份能力被拿掉了。

normal.en: Dis- not plus ability means the ability is missing.
normal.cn: dis-（不）加 ability 就是能力缺失。

normal.en: Disability is the noun, disabled the adjective.
normal.cn: disability 是名词，disabled 是形容词。

normal.en: Inability is plain lack; disability is a condition.
normal.cn: inability 是单纯做不到，disability 是一种状况。

normal.en: Disabilities is the plural for several conditions.
normal.cn: disabilities 是多种状况的复数。

normal.en: In law it can mean a bar on acting.
normal.cn: 在法律上它可指行为资格被剥夺。

abstract.en: A wheelchair at the foot of a smooth ramp beside a wide door button.
abstract.cn: 轮椅停在平缓坡道下，旁边是一个宽大的开门按钮。

abstract.en: A hand in a sling resting beside an unopened toolbox.
abstract.cn: 一只吊着绷带的手放在没打开的工具箱旁。

abstract.en: A contract with the signature line left blank and a stamp beside it.
abstract.cn: 一份合同的签名栏空着，旁边放着印章。

examples.en: She never treats her disability as a barrier.
examples.cn: 她从不把残疾当成障碍。

examples.en: The form asks whether you have a disability.
examples.cn: 表格询问你是否有残疾。

examples.en: The contract ended because of legal disability.
examples.cn: 合同因法律上的无行为能力而终止。

dict_mnemonic.text: disability ＝ dis-（不、剥夺）＋ ability（能力，源自拉丁语 habere「拥有、握住」→ habilis「顺手的」）＝「能力被拿掉」，指残疾、伤残；法律上又指无行为能力。形容词是 disabled。

root: 拉丁语 habere（拥有）→ habilis（顺手的）→ 古法语 able → 英语 ability ＋ dis-（否定）→ disability

sensesIntro.en: Capacity taken away: a ramp beside steps, a hand in a sling and a contract that cannot be signed.
sensesIntro.cn: 被拿走的能力：台阶旁的一段坡道、吊着绷带的手，以及一份签不了的合同。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wheelchair waiting at the foot of a smooth ramp next to a wide automatic door button
core.cn: 核心意象：轮椅等在一段平缓坡道下，旁边是宽大的自动门按钮

branches.en: A wheelchair at the foot of a smooth ramp beside a wide door button.
branches.cn: 轮椅停在平缓坡道下，旁边是一个宽大的开门按钮。

branches.en: A hand in a sling resting beside an unopened toolbox.
branches.cn: 一只吊着绷带的手放在没打开的工具箱旁。

branches.en: A contract with the signature line left blank and a stamp beside it.
branches.cn: 一份合同的签名栏空着，旁边放着印章。

branches.en: Both name a capacity that is not available.
branches.cn: 两者都指一份用不上的能力。

branches.en: Both stop an action from being completed.
branches.cn: 两者都让某个动作无法完成。

intro.en: Disability is dis- plus ability; the hold root also builds habit, capable and incapacity.
intro.cn: disability 由 dis- 加 ability 构成；握住这个词根也造出 habit、capable 与 incapacity。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere means to have or hold, habilis handy and pejor worse.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habere 意为拥有、握住，habilis 意为顺手的，pejor 意为更坏的。

definition_en: to stop a device or system from working, or to make someone unable to use part of the body
core_image: 一只手按下开关，屏幕上的一排按钮同时变成灰色
scene: 他蹲在机箱后面，把那根细线从接口里拔了出来。A single broken wire can disable the whole alarm.
sceneCN: 这里 disable 指「使失效」（第 1 个义项：让设备无法工作）；句意是一根断线就能让整套警报失灵。

senses.title: To put a machine out of action
senses.definition: to damage or switch off a device so that it cannot work
senses.definitionCN: 损坏或关掉设备，使它无法运转
senses.example: The storm disabled the power lines.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴让电线断了电。
senses.why: One small part stops, and everything that depended on it stops too.
senses.whyCN: 一个小零件停了，靠它运转的一切也跟着停。

senses.title: To take away bodily power
senses.definition: to make a person unable to move or use part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 使人无法活动或使用身体的某一部分
senses.example: A fall disabled him for several months.
senses.exampleCN: 一次摔倒让他几个月不能行动。
senses.why: The body is still there, but one road inside it is closed.
senses.whyCN: 身体还在，只是里面有一条路被封住了。

senses.title: To switch off a feature
senses.definition: to turn off an option or an account in a system
senses.definitionCN: 在系统里关掉某个选项或账号
senses.example: You can disable the camera in the settings.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以在设置里关掉相机。
senses.why: Nothing is broken; someone simply decides it will not answer.
senses.whyCN: 什么都没坏，只是有人决定让它不再回应。

intro.en: Disable joins the negative prefix dis- to able, and first meant to make someone unable in law.
intro.cn: disable 由否定前缀 dis- 加 able 构成，最初指使人在法律上失去资格。

items.en: Habilis meant easy to handle or fit for use.
items.cn: habilis 指好使唤的、合用的。

items.en: The prefix dis- reversed the quality, giving the sense of not able.
items.cn: 前缀 dis- 把这一性质反过来，给出「不能」的意思。

items.en: To disable first meant to make a person legally unable.
items.cn: disable 最初指使某人在法律上失去资格。

items.en: The word spread from people to machines and their parts.
items.cn: 这个词从人扩展到机器及其零件。

items.en: It now also means to switch off a software feature.
items.cn: 如今它也指关闭软件中的某项功能。

note.en: The look-alike group plays with able and its negation, while the meaning group names ways of stopping something.
note.cn: 形近组在 able 及其否定形式上做文章，近义组则列出几种让东西停下的说法。

entries.definition: to make someone or something able to do something
entries.definitionCN: 使某人或某物能够做某事

entries.definition: not having the power or chance to do something
entries.definitionCN: 没有能力或机会做某事

entries.definition: in a skilful and competent way
entries.definitionCN: 能干地；巧妙地

entries.definition: to make a device or system stop working
entries.definitionCN: 使设备或系统停止工作

entries.definition: to damage something so badly that it cannot work
entries.definitionCN: 严重损坏某物使其无法运作

entries.definition: to weaken a power or a function
entries.definitionCN: 削弱某种能力或功能

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a switch that will not move to a body that will not answer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从按不动的开关，走到不再回应的身体。

normal.en: Dis- means not, so disable means not able.
normal.cn: dis- 是「不」，disable 就是「不能」。

normal.en: One grey button can turn a whole machine off.
normal.cn: 一个变灰的按钮，就能让整台机器停下。

normal.en: A disabled account cannot log in.
normal.cn: 被停用的账号登不进去。

normal.en: A broken wire disables more than itself.
normal.cn: 一根断线停下的不只是它自己。

normal.en: The word takes away ability, not the thing itself.
normal.cn: 这个词拿走的是能力，不是东西本身。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pulling one small plug.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手拔掉一个小小的插头。

abstract.en: Picture a long row of lights going dark from left to right.
abstract.cn: 想象一排灯从左到右依次暗下去。

abstract.en: Picture a door that still stands but no longer opens.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门还在，却再也打不开。

examples.en: The storm disabled the power lines.
examples.cn: 风暴让电线断了电。

examples.en: A fall disabled him for several months.
examples.cn: 一次摔倒让他几个月不能行动。

examples.en: You can disable the camera in the settings.
examples.cn: 你可以在设置里关掉相机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disable 记成「敌塞包」：敌人往机器里塞了个包，机器就失效了。

root: 由否定前缀 dis- 加 able（能够）构成，字面就是「使不能」。十五世纪先指使人在法律上失去资格，后来泛指使人失去行动能力，现代又用于设备、账号与软件功能的失效。

sensesIntro.en: From a machine that stops, to a body that cannot answer, to a feature switched off in a menu.
sensesIntro.cn: 从停下的机器，到不听使唤的身体，再到菜单里被关掉的功能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one small plug pulled out, and everything behind it goes dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小小的插头被拔掉，后面的一切都暗了。

branches.en: The first sense is a device that can no longer work.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是再也无法工作的设备。

branches.en: The second sense is a body that can no longer move freely.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是再也无法自由活动的身体。

branches.en: The third sense is a feature that has been switched off.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是被关掉的一项功能。

branches.en: A dead machine and a grey button both lose their power to answer.
branches.cn: 停下的机器和变灰的按钮，都失去了回应的能力。

branches.en: In both cases the frame remains and the power is gone.
branches.cn: 两种情形里，架子都还在，力气却没了。

intro.en: Disable gathers the able family, words about power, skill and its loss.
intro.cn: disable 聚起 able 一族词，围绕能力、本领与失去。

latinIntro.en: Latin habilis, fit for use, gives able; the prefix dis- turns that fitness into its opposite.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habilis（合用）给出 able，前缀 dis- 又把这份能力翻转过来。

items.example: The crash disabled the control system.
items.exampleCN: 那次撞车让控制系统失灵了。

items.meaning: having the power or skill to do something
items.example: She was able to finish the work alone.
items.exampleCN: 她一个人就能干完这活。

items.meaning: the power or skill to do something

definition_en: to stop being seen, or to stop existing
core_image: 魔术师把布一掀，桌上的鸟笼空了，只剩一根羽毛
scene: 灯忽然灭了，台上的人影没了，观众还以为这是节目的一部分。The coin seemed to disappear between his fingers.
sceneCN: 这里 disappear 指「消失」（第 1 个义项：看不见了）；句意是那枚硬币在他指间好像消失了。

senses.title: Out of sight
senses.definition: to pass out of sight so that the eye can no longer find it
senses.definitionCN: 离开视线，眼睛再也找不到
senses.example: The coin seemed to disappear between his fingers.
senses.exampleCN: 那枚硬币在他指间好像消失了。
senses.why: What the eye cannot follow, the mind cannot keep.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛跟不上的东西，脑子也留不住。

senses.title: Missing without explanation
senses.definition: to be lost or to go missing, often leaving no trace
senses.definitionCN: 走失或不见，往往不留痕迹
senses.example: Two hikers disappeared in the fog.
senses.exampleCN: 两名徒步者在雾里失踪了。
senses.why: The empty place asks a question that has no answer yet.
senses.whyCN: 那块空出来的地方，问出一个还没有答案的问题。

senses.title: Gone for good
senses.definition: to stop existing, as a species or a custom does
senses.definitionCN: 像物种或习俗那样不再存在
senses.example: Many old crafts are disappearing from the village.
senses.exampleCN: 村里许多老手艺正在消失。
senses.why: The last one goes, and nothing in the world can be asked again.
senses.whyCN: 最后一个没了，世上就再没有谁可以问了。

intro.en: Disappear is dis- added to appear, which comes from Latin apparere, to come into sight.
intro.cn: disappear 是 dis- 加 appear，而 appear 来自拉丁语 apparere（出现在眼前）。

items.en: Apparere meant to come into view or become visible.
items.cn: apparere 指进入视野或变得可见。

items.en: The prefix ad- added the sense of coming toward a place.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 添上「朝某处而来」的意思。

items.en: Appear entered English meaning to come in sight.
items.cn: appear 进入英语，意为出现在眼前。

items.en: Disappear reversed it into going out of sight.
items.cn: disappear 把它反过来，表示离开视线。

items.en: The word widened to missing people and vanishing species.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到失踪的人与消失的物种。

note.en: The look-alike group plays with appear and its forms, while the meaning group names ways of leaving no trace.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 appear 及其形式，近义组则列出几种不留痕迹的离开。

entries.definition: to come into sight
entries.definitionCN: 出现在视野中

entries.definition: the act of coming into sight, or the way something looks
entries.definitionCN: 出现这一动作，或某物的外表

entries.definition: easy to see or understand, or seeming true
entries.definitionCN: 显而易见的，或表面看来如此的

entries.definition: to disappear suddenly and completely
entries.definitionCN: 突然而彻底地消失

entries.definition: to grow weaker until it cannot be seen
entries.definitionCN: 渐渐变弱直到看不见

entries.definition: to turn into vapour and vanish from sight
entries.definitionCN: 化为蒸气而从眼前消失

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a coin hidden in a palm to a craft that leaves a village for good.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从藏在掌心的硬币，走到永远离开村庄的手艺。

normal.en: Dis- means away, so disappear is to take away the appearance.
normal.cn: dis- 是「离开」，disappear 就是把出现带走。

normal.en: The coin disappears because the hand closes.
normal.cn: 硬币之所以不见，是因为手掌合上了。

normal.en: A person disappears when no one can say where.
normal.cn: 一个人失踪，是没人说得出他在哪儿。

normal.en: A custom disappears when the last hand stops doing it.
normal.cn: 一门习俗消失，是最后一双手不再做了。

normal.en: What disappears leaves an outline where it used to be.
normal.cn: 消失的东西，会在原来的位置留下一个轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture a palm opening over an empty table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手掌在空桌上摊开。

abstract.en: Picture fog closing over a path.
abstract.cn: 想象雾把小径合拢起来。

abstract.en: Picture a birdcage with the door open and no bird.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸟笼门开着，里面没有鸟。

examples.en: The sun disappeared behind the hills.
examples.cn: 太阳落到山后不见了。

examples.en: Her bag disappeared from the table.
examples.cn: 她的包从桌上不见了。

examples.en: Whole species are disappearing as the forest shrinks.
examples.cn: 随着森林缩小，整个物种正在消失。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disappear 记成「的士皮儿」：的士一开走，扬起的皮儿都散了，人影也没了。

root: 由否定前缀 dis- 加 appear 构成。appear 来自拉丁语 apparere（出现在眼前），词根 parere 意为露面。加前缀后表示离开视线，后来又从「看不见」扩展到「失踪」与「彻底不存在」。

sensesIntro.en: From a coin lost between fingers, to a person lost in fog, to a whole species lost for good.
sensesIntro.cn: 从指间不见的硬币，到雾里失踪的人，再到永远消失的整个物种。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open palm over an empty table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只摊开的手掌下面，桌子空了。

chain: THE HAND CLOSES OVER A COIN

branches.en: The first sense is simply being out of sight.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是单纯地离开视线。

branches.en: The second sense is a person no one can locate.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是没人找得到的人。

branches.en: The third sense is a kind of thing gone from the world.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是从世上消失的一类东西。

branches.en: A hidden coin and a missing walker both leave a searching eye.
branches.cn: 藏起的硬币和失踪的行人，都留下一双寻找的眼睛。

branches.en: One is lost for a while; the other is lost for good.
branches.cn: 一个只是暂时丢了，另一个是永远没了。

intro.en: Disappear belongs to the appear family, words about coming into view and leaving it.
intro.cn: disappear 属于 appear 一族，围绕出现与离开视线。

latinIntro.en: Latin apparere, to come into sight, is the source of appear and of disappear.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 apparere（出现在眼前）是 appear 与 disappear 的源头。

items.example: The ship disappeared into the mist.
A light appeared at the end of the road.
items.exampleCN: 路尽头出现了一点灯光。

items.meaning: the act of appearing or the look of a thing
items.example: His sudden appearance surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 他的突然出现让我们吃了一惊。

items.meaning: easy to see or seeming to be true
items.example: It was apparent that she had been crying.

items.meaning: as far as one can see or judge
items.example: Apparently the shop closed last month.
items.exampleCN: 那家店看来上个月就关了。

items.meaning: the act of vanishing or being lost
items.example: The police studied his sudden disappearance.
items.exampleCN: 警方调查他的突然失踪。

items.example: The moon reappeared after the clouds passed.
items.exampleCN: 云过去后月亮又出来了。

items.meaning: in the act of going out of sight
items.example: He watched the disappearing shore.
items.exampleCN: 他望着渐渐消失的海岸。

definition_zh: 使失望；使希望落空；使受挫
definition_en: to fail to satisfy someone's hope or expectation
core_image: 拆开的礼物盒里躺着一张写错的卡片，孩子的笑停在半路
scene: 他拆开信封，看了两行就把它折回去。The ending disappointed everyone who had waited a year.
sceneCN: 这里 disappointed 指「使失望」（第 1 个义项：没能满足期待）；句意是那个结局让等了一年的人都失望了。

derivatives.zh: 失望；令人失望的人或事

senses.title: To let someone down
senses.definition: to make a person feel sad because what was hoped for did not happen
senses.definitionCN: 因所盼望的没有实现而让人难过
senses.example: The ending disappointed everyone who had waited a year.
senses.exampleCN: 那个结局让等了一年的人都失望了。
senses.why: The picture in the mind was brighter than the thing in the hand.
senses.whyCN: 脑子里的画面，比手里拿到的东西更亮。

senses.title: To fall short of a hope
senses.definition: to fail to reach the standard that was expected
senses.definitionCN: 没有达到所期待的水平
senses.example: The film disappointed the hopes of its young fans.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影让年轻影迷的希望落了空。
senses.why: A promise is measured only after it has been kept or broken.
senses.whyCN: 承诺只有在守住或落空之后，才量得出长短。

senses.title: To defeat a plan
senses.definition: to prevent a plan or purpose from being carried out
senses.definitionCN: 使计划或目的无法实现
senses.example: Heavy rain disappointed our plan for the day.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨打乱了当天的计划。
senses.why: A plan can be broken by weather as easily as by a person.
senses.whyCN: 计划能被一个人打破，也能被一场雨打破。

intro.en: Disappoint came from Old French desappointer, to remove from a post, built on point, a fixed place.
intro.cn: disappoint 来自古法语 desappointer（免职），词基 point 指固定的位置。

items.en: Punctum meant a point or a small hole, the base of point.
items.cn: punctum 指点或小孔，是 point 的词源。

items.en: Apointier meant to arrange or to set a matter in place.
items.cn: apointier 指安排妥当，把事情放到位置上。

items.en: Desappointer meant to remove someone from an appointment.
items.cn: desappointer 指解除某人的职位。

items.en: English used disappoint for removing a person from office.
items.cn: 英语最初用 disappoint 表示免除某人的职务。

items.en: The sense shifted from losing a post to losing a hope.
items.cn: 词义从失去职位，转向失去一份期待。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the appoint stem, while the meaning group names other ways of failing a hope.
note.cn: 形近组共用 appoint 这一段词干，近义组则列出其他让希望落空的方式。

entries.definition: to choose someone for a job or position
entries.definitionCN: 选某人担任某职

entries.definition: a fixed time to meet, or a job given to someone
entries.definitionCN: 约定的会面时间，或授予的职位

entries.definition: sad because a hope was not met
entries.definitionCN: 因希望未实现而难过的

entries.definition: to fail to help or support someone who trusted you
entries.definitionCN: 辜负信任自己的人

entries.definition: to prevent a hope or plan from succeeding
entries.definitionCN: 使希望或计划无法实现

entries.definition: to make someone feel shock and loss of hope
entries.definitionCN: 使某人震惊并失去希望

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a gift that misses its mark to a plan broken by rain.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从没送到心上的礼物，走到被雨打乱的计划。

normal.en: Dis- plus appoint: the appointment is taken away.
normal.cn: dis- 加 appoint：本来说好的位置被拿走了。

normal.en: A gift that misses the wish disappoints the hand.
normal.cn: 送不到心愿上的礼物，会让接的手失望。

normal.en: Disappointed is the face; disappointing is the cause.
normal.cn: disappointed 是那张脸，disappointing 是那个原因。

normal.en: A film can disappoint a whole row of fans at once.
normal.cn: 一部电影能同时让一整排影迷失望。

normal.en: The word once meant losing a post, now it means losing a hope.
normal.cn: 这个词从前指丢了职位，如今指丢了希望。

abstract.en: Picture a gift box open with the wrong card inside.
abstract.cn: 想象礼盒打开，里面放错了卡片。

abstract.en: Picture a smile that stops halfway.
abstract.cn: 想象一个笑到一半停住的表情。

abstract.en: Picture a paper plan soaked by rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被雨泡软的计划纸。

examples.en: I did not mean to disappoint you.
examples.cn: 我不是有意让你失望。

examples.en: The result disappointed everyone in the team.
examples.cn: 结果让队里每个人都失望了。

examples.en: His second book disappointed the critics.
examples.cn: 他的第二本书让评论界失望了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disappoint 记成「的士破印」：约好的的士没来，车票上的印也破了，等的人自然失望。

root: 来自古法语 desappointer，本义是解除某人的职位，词基 point 指点、位置，出自拉丁语 punctum。进入英语后先表示免职，后来词义转向「使期待落空」，因为失去职位正是最直接的失望。

sensesIntro.en: From a person whose hope is not met, to a standard that is not reached, to a plan that cannot go on.
sensesIntro.cn: 从希望没被满足的人，到没达到的标准，再到无法继续的计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gift box open, and the card inside says the wrong name.
core.cn: 核心意象：礼盒打开，里面的卡片写着错的名字。

branches.en: The first sense is the person whose hope is let down.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是希望被辜负的那个人。

branches.en: The second sense is the standard that is not reached.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是没能达到的那条标准。

branches.en: The third sense is the plan that cannot move forward.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是走不下去的计划。

branches.en: A person and a promise are judged by the same gap.
branches.cn: 人和承诺，都是用同一道落差来衡量的。

branches.en: A hope and a plan both end where reality refuses them.
branches.cn: 希望和计划，都停在现实不答应的地方。

intro.en: Disappoint gathers the appoint family, words about posts, promises and let-downs.
intro.cn: disappoint 聚起 appoint 一族词，围绕职位、约定与辜负。

latinIntro.en: Point and appoint go back to Latin punctum, a point or a fixed place.
latinIntro.cn: point 与 appoint 都可追到拉丁语 punctum（点、固定位置）。

items.meaning: to fail to meet a hope
items.example: The news disappointed the whole family.

items.meaning: to choose someone for a post
items.example: They appointed her as head of the team.
items.exampleCN: 他们任命她为团队负责人。

items.meaning: a fixed meeting or a post given to someone
items.example: I have an appointment at four.
She looked disappointed by the answer.
It was a disappointing season.
items.exampleCN: 那是个令人失望的赛季。

items.meaning: the feeling of being let down
items.example: He hid his disappointment well.

items.meaning: in a way that lets people down
items.example: The machine worked disappointingly slowly.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器慢得让人失望。

items.meaning: to choose someone for a post again
items.example: The board reappointed him for two years.

definition_en: to think that something is wrong or unacceptable
core_image: 一只手在桌下轻轻摆了摆，示意别再往下说
scene: 他刚提到辞职，母亲就放下了手里的针线。My father disapproves of late nights.
sceneCN: 这里 disapproves 指「不赞成」（第 1 个义项：认为不妥）；句意是我父亲不赞成熬夜。

senses.title: To judge an act as wrong
senses.definition: to think that a person's behaviour is not acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 认为某人的行为不可接受
senses.example: My father disapproves of late nights.
senses.exampleCN: 我父亲不赞成熬夜。
senses.why: The judgement comes first, and the sentence comes after.
senses.whyCN: 判断先到，话后到。

senses.title: To be against an idea
senses.definition: to think that a plan or idea should not go forward
senses.definitionCN: 认为某个计划或想法不该推进
senses.example: Most of the staff disapproved of the new rule.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数员工反对这条新规定。
senses.why: A plan is stopped in the mind before it is stopped in the office.
senses.whyCN: 计划先在脑子里被拦下，才在办公室里被拦下。

senses.title: To refuse official consent
senses.definition: to officially decide not to accept a request or a budget
senses.definitionCN: 正式决定不接受某项请求或预算
senses.example: The committee disapproved the new budget.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会没有批准新预算。
senses.why: The same judgement, once signed, closes a door.
senses.whyCN: 同一种判断，一签上字就关上了一扇门。

intro.en: Disapprove is dis- plus approve, whose Latin base approbare meant to test something as good.
intro.cn: disapprove 是 dis- 加 approve，其拉丁词基 approbare 指检验后认为好。

items.en: Probare meant to test, to prove or to judge.
items.cn: probare 指检验、证明或判断。

items.en: Approbare added ad- and meant to approve a thing.
items.cn: approbare 加上 ad-，表示认可某物。

items.en: Approve entered English with the sense of proving or commending.
items.cn: approve 进入英语时，指证明或称赞。

items.en: Disapprove reversed the judgement into a refusal.
items.cn: disapprove 把这份认可反转为否定。

items.en: The verb now covers private views and official decisions.
items.cn: 这个词既指私下看法，也指官方决定。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the approve stem, while the meaning group names other ways of saying no.
note.cn: 形近组共用 approve 这一段词干，近义组则列出其他说「不」的方式。

entries.definition: to think that something is good
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事好

entries.definition: a favourable judgement or consent
entries.definitionCN: 赞许的判断或同意

entries.definition: a judgement that something is wrong
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事不妥的判断

entries.definition: to say that one is against something
entries.definitionCN: 表示反对某事

entries.definition: to act against a plan or a person
entries.definitionCN: 采取行动反对某计划或某人

entries.definition: to regard something with clear disapproval
entries.definitionCN: 对某事明显不赞成

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a hand waved under a table to a stamp that is never given.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从桌下摆了一下的手，走到始终没有盖下的那枚章。

normal.en: Dis- plus approve: the approval is refused.
normal.cn: dis- 加 approve：认可被拒绝。

normal.en: A father disapproves with a look before a word.
normal.cn: 父亲往往先用眼神表示不赞成，然后才开口。

normal.en: Disapprove of a habit, and you judge the act, not the person.
normal.cn: 不赞成一种习惯，评的是行为，不是人。

normal.en: A committee can disapprove a budget with one vote.
normal.cn: 委员会一次投票就能不批准预算。

normal.en: The word leaves the thing standing, but withholds the yes.
normal.cn: 这个词让事情立着，却把那个「同意」扣下了。

abstract.en: Picture a hand waving low, out of sight.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在低处、在别人看不见的地方摆了摆。

abstract.en: Picture lips pressed while the eyes stay steady.
abstract.cn: 想象嘴唇抿紧，眼睛却一动不动。

abstract.en: Picture a form returned without a signature.
abstract.cn: 想象一份表格被退回，上面没有签名。

examples.en: My father disapproves of late nights.
examples.cn: 我父亲不赞成熬夜。

examples.en: The committee disapproved the new budget.
examples.cn: 委员会没有批准新预算。

examples.en: She disapproved of the way he spoke to the waiter.
examples.cn: 她不赞成他那样跟服务员说话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disapprove 记成「的士不认」：司机不认这条路，摆手说不，就是不赞成。

root: 由否定前缀 dis- 加 approve 构成。approve 来自拉丁语 approbare（检验后认为好），词根 probare 意为检验、证明。加前缀后表示认为某事不妥，既可指私下的态度，也可指公开反对，甚至正式不予批准。

sensesIntro.en: From a private judgement of an act, to opposition to an idea, to an official no.
sensesIntro.cn: 从对行为的私下判断，到对想法的反对，再到官方的一声「不」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand waved low, telling someone to stop.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在低处摆动，示意停下。

branches.en: The first sense is a judgement of behaviour.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是对行为的判断。

branches.en: The second sense is a stand against an idea.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是对某个想法的抵制。

branches.en: The third sense is the official refusal to consent.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是官方拒绝同意。

branches.en: A habit and a plan can both meet the same closed face.
branches.cn: 一种习惯和一个计划，可能撞上同一张合起来的脸。

branches.en: A spoken no becomes a formal no once it is recorded.
branches.cn: 说出的「不」一旦被记下，就成了正式的「不」。

intro.en: Disapprove belongs to the approve family, words about judging and consenting.
intro.cn: disapprove 属于 approve 一族，围绕评判与同意。

latinIntro.en: Latin probare, to test or prove, gives the prove in approve and disapprove.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 probare（检验、证明）给出 approve 与 disapprove 里的 prove。

items.example: They disapprove of the way the land is used.
items.exampleCN: 他们不赞成这块地的用法。

items.example: The board approved the design.
items.exampleCN: 董事会批准了这个设计。

items.example: The plan is waiting for approval.

items.meaning: a judgement that something is wrong
items.example: His silence was a form of disapproval.
items.exampleCN: 他的沉默就是一种不赞成。

items.example: She gave an approving smile.
The teacher gave a disapproving look.
items.exampleCN: 老师投来不以为然的目光。

items.meaning: in a way that shows approval
items.example: He nodded approvingly at the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他赞许地对方案点了点头。

items.meaning: in a way that shows disapproval

definition_en: an event that causes great damage or suffering, or a complete failure
core_image: 风暴过后，屋顶掀开一半，一把椅子挂在树枝上
scene: 水退到脚踝，墙上留着一条深色的线，家具全倒了。The flood was the worst disaster in the town's history.
sceneCN: 这里 disaster 指「灾难」（第 1 个义项：造成巨大损失的事件）；句意是这场洪水是该镇历史上最严重的灾难。

senses.title: An event of great harm
senses.definition: a sudden event such as a flood or fire that causes great damage
senses.definitionCN: 洪水、火灾之类突然造成巨大损失的事件
senses.example: The flood was the worst disaster in the town's history.
senses.exampleCN: 这场洪水是该镇历史上最严重的灾难。
senses.why: The world keeps its shape, but people lose theirs.
senses.whyCN: 世界还保持着形状，人的日子却散了。

senses.title: A complete failure
senses.definition: a plan or event that fails completely
senses.definitionCN: 彻底失败的计划或活动
senses.example: The concert was a disaster from the first note.
senses.exampleCN: 那场音乐会从第一个音起就是一场灾难。
senses.why: Nobody is hurt, and yet everything has fallen down.
senses.whyCN: 没有人受伤，可所有东西都塌了。

senses.title: A hopeless person
senses.definition: a person who is completely unable to do something well
senses.definitionCN: 完全做不好某件事的人
senses.example: He is a disaster in the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 他在厨房里简直一塌糊涂。
senses.why: The word lends its ruin to one clumsy pair of hands.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把自己的废墟，借给了一双笨手。

intro.en: Disaster came from Italian disastro, literally an ill star, and carried the old belief that stars shaped events.
intro.cn: disaster 来自意大利语 disastro，字面是「凶星」，带着星辰左右世事的旧观念。

items.en: Astrum meant a star, and astronomy read the sky for signs.
items.cn: astrum 指星辰，占星与天象之学都从天上找征兆。

items.en: Disastro joined dis-, bad, to astro, star.
items.cn: disastro 把表示「坏」的 dis- 与 astro（星）合在一起。

items.en: Desastre carried the word into French with the same sense.
items.cn: desastre 以同样的意思把词带进法语。

items.en: English disaster named a calamity blamed on an unlucky star.
items.cn: 英语 disaster 指归咎于凶星的灾祸。

items.en: The star faded, and the word kept only the ruin.
items.cn: 星辰的意味淡去，这个词只留下了废墟。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by a letter or two, while the meaning group names other large misfortunes.
note.cn: 形近组只差一两个字母，近义组则列出其他巨大的不幸。

entries.definition: a large dry area of land with little rain
entries.definitionCN: 雨水稀少的干旱大地

entries.definition: sweet food eaten at the end of a meal
entries.definitionCN: 餐后吃的甜食

entries.definition: causing great harm or failure
entries.definitionCN: 造成巨大损害或失败的

entries.definition: an event that causes great and sudden suffering
entries.definitionCN: 造成巨大而突然苦难的事件

entries.definition: a serious misfortune that brings deep distress
entries.definitionCN: 带来深切痛苦的严重不幸

entries.definition: a very sad event, especially one involving death
entries.definitionCN: 极悲惨的事件，尤指涉及死亡的

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a storm over a town to a kitchen ruined by one cook.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从笼罩小镇的风暴，走到被一个厨子弄乱的厨房。

normal.en: Dis- plus aster: a bad star was once blamed for every ruin.
normal.cn: dis- 加 aster：从前每场废墟都怪一颗凶星。

normal.en: A natural disaster arrives without asking.
normal.cn: 自然灾害从不先打招呼。

normal.en: A party can be a disaster and still be remembered fondly.
normal.cn: 一场聚会可能是灾难，却仍被人笑着记住。

normal.en: Disaster relief arrives after the water, not before.
normal.cn: 救灾总是在水来之后，而不是之前。

normal.en: One clumsy cook can turn a kitchen into a disaster area.
normal.cn: 一个笨厨子就能把厨房变成灾区。

abstract.en: Picture a roof half lifted off a house.
abstract.cn: 想象屋顶被掀开了一半。

abstract.en: Picture a chair hanging from a tree branch.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子挂在树枝上。

abstract.en: Picture a dark line left high on a wall by water.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上高处留着一条水退后的深色线。

examples.en: The earthquake was a disaster for the whole region.
examples.cn: 这场地震对整个地区是一场灾难。

examples.en: Poor planning turned the event into a disaster.
examples.cn: 糟糕的筹划把这场活动变成了灾难。

examples.en: Several disasters struck the coast that year.
examples.cn: 那一年海岸遭遇了好几次灾害。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disaster 记成「地砸死他」：地一塌，砸下来，就是一场灾难。

root: 来自意大利语 disastro，字面意思是「凶星」，由表示坏的 dis- 与 astro（星辰）组成。古人相信星辰决定祸福，于是把大祸归因于星象。这个词经法语进入英语后，星辰的意味逐渐淡去，只留下灾难与彻底失败的意思。

sensesIntro.en: From a flood that ruins a town, to an evening that ruins itself, to a cook who ruins dinner.
sensesIntro.cn: 从毁掉小镇的洪水，到自我毁掉的夜晚，再到毁掉晚饭的厨子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a house with its roof half gone and a chair in the tree.
core.cn: 核心意象：屋顶没了一半，椅子挂在树上。

branches.en: The first sense is the great event that harms many.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是伤害许多人的巨大事件。

branches.en: The second sense is a failure with no injury.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是没有伤人却彻底失败的事。

branches.en: The third sense lends that ruin to one hopeless person.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把这片废墟借给一个没救的人。

branches.en: A flood and a concert can both end in the same wreckage.
branches.cn: 洪水和音乐会，都可能收在同样的残局里。

branches.en: A failed evening and a failing cook share one word.
branches.cn: 失败的夜晚和失败的厨子，共用一个词。

intro.en: Disaster opens the star family: disaster, disastrous, and the astro- words.
intro.cn: disaster 打开了「星辰」一族：disaster、disastrous 以及 astro 系列。

latinIntro.en: Latin astrum, star, and Greek astron, star, give the astro- base in this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 astrum 与希腊语 astron 都指星辰，给出这一族的 astro 词基。

items.example: The fire was a disaster for the village.

items.meaning: a small rocky body in space

definition_en: a flat round object, a disc that stores sound or data, or a pad between bones

scene: 唱机的手臂落下，圆盘开始转，屋里响起沙沙的底噪。He slid the disc into the player.

senses.title: A round carrier of sound or data
senses.definition: a thin round object on which music or computer data is stored

senses.example: He slid the disc into the player.

senses.why: A whole evening of sound hides in one shiny circle.

senses.why: Even the body keeps small round cushions between hard parts.

intro.en: Disc goes back through Latin discus to Greek diskos, a flat round plate thrown in games.

items.en: Diskos named a quoit, a flat stone or metal plate thrown in sport.
items.cn: diskos 指比赛里掷出的扁石盘或金属盘。

items.en: Discus borrowed the Greek word for the same object.
items.cn: discus 借来这个希腊词，指同样的东西。

items.en: Disc and disk entered English for a flat round surface.
items.cn: disc 与 disk 进入英语，指扁平的圆面。

root: 来自希腊语 diskos（掷出的扁圆盘），经拉丁语 discus 进入英语，最初指扁平的圆面。后来唱片、激光光盘先后借用这个词，使它有了承载声音与数据的意思；医学上又用它指脊椎骨之间的软垫。

sensesIntro.en: From a shiny circle that holds music, to any flat round plate, to a cushion inside the spine.
sensesIntro.cn: 从装着音乐的亮圆片，到任何扁圆盘，再到脊椎里的软垫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin round plate spinning under a light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片薄圆盘在灯下旋转。

chain: DATA IS BURNED IN TINY DOTS
A SOFT PAD SITS BETWEEN BONES

branches.en: The first sense is the round carrier of sound or data.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是承载声音或数据的圆片。

branches.en: The second sense is the bare shape itself.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是那个形状本身。

branches.en: The third sense is the body's own small disc.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是身体里自带的小圆盘。

branches.en: Music and metal both borrow the same flat circle.
branches.cn: 音乐与金属借用了同一个扁圆。

branches.en: A pad between bones is a disc no one can see.
branches.cn: 骨间的软垫，是一只看不见的圆盘。

intro.en: Disc gathers a family of round and flat words, from disks to discus.
intro.cn: disc 聚起一族与圆、扁有关的词，从磁盘到铁饼。

latinIntro.en: Greek diskos and Latin discus, a thrown plate, give the base disc-.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 diskos 与拉丁语 discus（掷出的圆盘）给出词基 disc。

items.example: The disc lay face down on the desk.
items.exampleCN: 那张光盘正面朝下放在桌上。

items.meaning: a flat round object or storage device
items.example: The file is saved on the disk.
The party played disco all night.
items.exampleCN: 聚会整晚都在放迪斯科。

items.meaning: a heavy disc thrown in sport
items.example: He threw the discus across the field.

items.meaning: a person who plays recorded music
items.example: The disc jockey kept the crowd dancing.
items.exampleCN: 唱片骑师让全场一直跳着。

items.meaning: a machine part that reads discs
items.example: The disc drive would not open.

items.meaning: brakes that press on a round plate
items.example: The bike has disc brakes on both wheels.
items.exampleCN: 这辆车的两个轮子都装了盘式刹车。

items.meaning: having the form of a flat circle
items.example: The nest was disc-shaped and shallow.

definition_en: to throw something away because it is no longer wanted
core_image: 楼道口一只旧沙发，坐垫裂开，露出里面的黄海绵
scene: 搬家的人把旧箱子一件件抬到楼下，堆在墙边。They discarded the broken chairs behind the shop.
sceneCN: 这里 discarded 指「丢弃」（第 1 个义项：当作没用的东西扔掉）；句意是他们把坏椅子扔在店后面。

senses.title: To throw an object away
senses.definition: to get rid of something that is broken or no longer wanted
senses.definitionCN: 把坏掉或不再需要的东西处理掉
senses.example: They discarded the broken chairs behind the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把坏椅子扔在店后面。
senses.why: The hand lets go, and the object becomes someone else's problem.
senses.whyCN: 手一松，那件东西就成了别人的麻烦。

senses.title: To give up an idea or plan
senses.definition: to stop considering a plan or belief as useful
senses.definitionCN: 不再认为某个计划或想法有用
senses.example: The team discarded the first design.
senses.exampleCN: 团队放弃了第一版设计。
senses.why: An idea can be dropped as easily as a torn coat.
senses.whyCN: 一个想法，可以像破外套一样被丢下。

senses.title: To lay down a card
senses.definition: to put down a card that is no longer needed in a game
senses.definitionCN: 在牌局中打出不再需要的牌
senses.example: He discarded a low card and kept the ace.
senses.exampleCN: 他打出一张小牌，留下了爱司。
senses.why: What leaves the hand still lies on the table.
senses.whyCN: 离开手的东西，仍旧躺在桌上。

intro.en: Discard is dis-, away, plus card, a piece of stiff paper, and first meant to throw out a card.
intro.cn: discard 是 dis-（离开）加 card（硬纸片），最初指把牌打出去。

items.en: Charta meant paper or a written sheet.
items.cn: charta 指纸或写字的纸页。

items.en: Carta named a playing card in Italian games.
items.cn: carta 在意大利的牌戏里指一张牌。

items.en: Carte carried the same sense into French card games.
items.cn: carte 把同样的意思带进法国牌戏。

items.en: To discard was to throw a card out of the hand.
items.cn: discard 最初指把一张牌从手里打出去。

items.en: The verb widened to any object or idea thrown away.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到任何被扔掉的东西或想法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the disc- opening, while the meaning group names other ways of letting things go.
note.cn: 形近组共用 disc 这一开头，近义组则列出其他放手的方式。

entries.definition: disagreement or a harsh mixture of sounds
entries.definitionCN: 不合，或刺耳的声音混杂

entries.definition: a style of dance music with a strong beat
entries.definitionCN: 节奏强烈的迪斯科舞曲

entries.definition: a heavy disc thrown in athletics
entries.definitionCN: 田径比赛中掷出的重圆盘

entries.definition: to get rid of something in a careless way
entries.definitionCN: 随便地把东西处理掉

entries.definition: to leave something behind for good
entries.definitionCN: 把某物永久地留下不管

entries.definition: to cancel or throw out something useless
entries.definitionCN: 取消或扔掉无用的东西

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a chair left by a wall to a card laid on a table.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从靠墙丢下的椅子，走到摊在桌上的一张牌。

normal.en: Dis- plus card: the card leaves the hand.
normal.cn: dis- 加 card：那张牌离开了手。

normal.en: Old chairs are discarded where nobody has to look.
normal.cn: 旧椅子总被丢在没人愿意看的地方。

normal.en: A plan can be discarded before it costs a penny.
normal.cn: 一个计划可以在花一分钱之前就被放弃。

normal.en: In a card game, discarding is a way of choosing.
normal.cn: 在牌局里，打出一张牌也是一种选择。

normal.en: What is discarded is not always worthless.
normal.cn: 被丢掉的东西，并不总是没有价值。

abstract.en: Picture a sofa with its cushion split open.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沙发的坐垫裂开了。

abstract.en: Picture a box left against a wall in the rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一只箱子被丢在墙边淋雨。

abstract.en: Picture one card sliding face up across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一张牌正面朝上滑过桌面。

examples.en: They discarded the broken chairs behind the shop.
examples.cn: 他们把坏椅子扔在店后面。

examples.en: The team discarded the first design.
examples.cn: 团队放弃了第一版设计。

examples.en: He discarded a low card and kept the ace.
examples.cn: 他打出一张小牌，留下了爱司。

root: 由表示「离开」的 dis- 加 card（纸牌）构成，字面就是「把牌打出去」。这个词先用于牌戏，指打出不要的牌；后来扩展到把旧物扔掉，再进一步指放弃想法、计划或习惯。

sensesIntro.en: From a broken chair left by a wall, to an idea dropped by a team, to a card laid on the table.
sensesIntro.cn: 从墙边丢下的坏椅子，到团队放弃的想法，再到摊在桌上的牌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand opening and letting an object fall away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手松开，让东西落下去。

chain: A HAND HOLDS AN OLD CHAIR

branches.en: The first sense is an object thrown away.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是被扔掉的实物。

branches.en: The second sense is an idea given up.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是被放弃的想法。

branches.en: The third sense is a card put down in a game.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是牌局里打出的一张牌。

branches.en: Things and plans both become lighter once dropped.
branches.cn: 东西和计划一旦丢下，都会变轻。

branches.en: A thrown chair and a played card both leave the hand.
branches.cn: 扔掉的椅子和打出的牌，都离开了手。

intro.en: Discard belongs to the card family, words about paper, maps and games.
intro.cn: discard 属于 card 一族，围绕纸片、图与牌戏。

latinIntro.en: Latin charta, paper, gives card and its relatives, including discard.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 charta（纸）给出 card 及其亲属词，包括 discard。

items.example: Do not discard the receipt.
She wrote the address on a card.
items.exampleCN: 她把地址写在一张卡片上。

items.meaning: thick stiff paper used for boxes
items.example: The books came in a cardboard box.
The chart shows the rise in prices.
items.exampleCN: 图表显示了物价的上涨。

items.example: The city was founded by royal charter.
items.exampleCN: 这座城依王室特许状建立。

items.example: The cups are cheap and discardable.
items.exampleCN: 这些杯子便宜，用完就可扔。

items.example: A discarded tyre lay in the ditch.
items.exampleCN: 一条被丢弃的轮胎躺在沟里。

items.example: Discarding old files saves space.
items.exampleCN: 清理旧文件能省出空间。

definition_zh: 辨明；看出；识别（细微差别）
definition_en: to see or understand something that is faint, hidden or not immediately obvious
core_image: 雾里一盏灯的轮廓慢慢从灰白中浮出来，眼睛要先分开背景才看得见它
scene: 天还没亮，守望的人从雾里辨认出远处灯塔的轮廓。In the fog the lookout discerned the outline of the lighthouse.
sceneCN: 这里指从模糊的背景中看出某物的轮廓（第 1 个义项：看清隐约或部分被遮住的东西）；句意：守望的人在雾中辨认出灯塔的轮廓。

senses.title: To perceive something faint or partly hidden
senses.titleCN: 看清隐约或被遮住之物
senses.definition: to make out an object or a sign that is dim, distant or partly concealed
senses.definitionCN: 辨认出模糊、遥远或部分被遮蔽的物体或迹象
senses.example: In the fog the lookout discerned the outline of the lighthouse.
senses.exampleCN: 守望的人在雾中辨认出灯塔的轮廓。
senses.why: The root means to sift, so seeing here is separating an object from the background that hides it.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为筛分，因此这里的看见是把物体从遮蔽它的背景中分开。

senses.title: To tell two similar things apart
senses.definition: to recognize the difference between things that look or sound alike
senses.definitionCN: 认出看起来或听起来相像之物间的差别
senses.example: A trained ear can discern the two instruments in the recording.
senses.exampleCN: 受过训练的耳朵能听出录音中的两件乐器。
senses.why: Sifting is choosing between pieces, and choosing between similar things is the same gesture applied to perception.
senses.whyCN: 筛分就是在碎片之间挑选，在相似之物间作选择是同一动作用在感知上。

senses.title: To judge wisely and see the truth
senses.definition: to understand a situation correctly, especially where others are misled
senses.definitionCN: 正确理解某种处境，尤其在旁人被误导之时
senses.example: She discerned the real reason behind the polite refusal.
senses.exampleCN: 她看出了那道客气拒绝背后的真正原因。
senses.why: Clear sight is used of the mind as well as the eye, so judgement becomes a kind of seeing.
senses.whyCN: 清晰的目光既用于眼睛，也用于心智，因此判断成为一种看见。

senses.title: To notice a pattern or trend
senses.definition: to detect a regularity that is not obvious from a single case
senses.definitionCN: 从单个事例中看不出、但能被察觉的规律性
senses.example: Analysts discern a slow shift in consumer habits.
senses.exampleCN: 分析人士看出一股消费者习惯上的缓慢变化。
senses.why: A pattern is hidden in the mass of details, and the verb names the act of separating it out.
senses.whyCN: 模式藏在大量细节里，这个动词命名的是把它分离出来的动作。

senses.title: To read someone's motives
senses.definition: to perceive what a person really intends beneath what is said
senses.definitionCN: 在所说出的话之下察觉某人真正的意图
senses.example: He could discern a little envy in her congratulations.
senses.exampleCN: 他能从她的祝贺中察觉出一点嫉妒。
senses.why: Human motives are faint signals, which is exactly what this verb is built to pick out.
senses.whyCN: 人的动机是微弱的信号，这正是这个动词生来要捕捉的东西。

senses.title: To tell right from wrong
senses.definition: to distinguish morally good conduct from bad without confusing the two
senses.definitionCN: 分清道德上的善与恶，不把两者混淆
senses.example: The old stories teach children to discern right from wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 这些古老的故事教孩子明辨是非。
senses.why: Moral judgement is described as seeing clearly, since the failure involved is a failure to distinguish.
senses.whyCN: 道德判断被描述成看得清楚，因为这里的失误就是分辨不清。

senses.title: To distinguish slight sensory differences
senses.definition: to notice small differences in taste, smell, colour or texture
senses.definitionCN: 察觉味道、气味、颜色或质地上的细微差异
senses.example: Few tasters can discern the difference between the two teas.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有品茶者能辨出这两种茶的差别。
senses.why: The senses are the original training ground for sifting, and fine tasting is its most literal survival.
senses.whyCN: 感官本是筛分能力最初的训练场，精细品鉴是它最字面的留存。

senses.title: To find structure in data or noise
senses.titleCN: 从数据或噪声中找出结构
senses.definition: to detect a real signal inside a mass of random or confusing information
senses.definitionCN: 在一大堆随机或混乱的信息中察觉真实的信号
senses.example: The software discerns a weak signal beneath the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 这套软件在噪声之下辨出一个微弱信号。
senses.why: Modern research is a new field for an old act: separating a signal from everything that covers it.
senses.whyCN: 现代研究给古老动作提供了新场地：把信号从覆盖它的一切中分离出来。

intro.en: Discern comes from a Latin verb meaning to separate and so to distinguish, built from a prefix of separation and a verb for sifting. English took it through French in the fourteenth century, and its noun became the ordinary word for judgement.
intro.cn: 本词出自一个表示分开、因而表示辨别的拉丁动词，由表示分离的前缀与表示筛分的动词构成。英语在十四世纪经法语借入，其名词后来成为表示判断力的常用词。

items.en: Cernere meant to sift or to separate, and from that came the sense of distinguishing one thing from another.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为筛分、分开，由此产生把一物与另一物区别开来的含义。

items.en: The prefix meant apart, so the compound pictured taking one thing out of a mixture.
items.cn: 这个前缀表示分开，因此复合词描绘的是把某物从混合物中取出来。

items.en: The Latin verb meant to separate, to distinguish and to perceive clearly.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为分开、区别、看清。

items.en: Old French carried the verb to English in the fourteenth century, where it settled in both sight and judgement.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把这个动词带到英语，它在视觉与判断两方面都站稳了脚。

items.en: The English noun became the fixed word for good judgement, especially in moral and practical matters.
items.cn: 英语名词成为表示良好判断力的固定说法，尤其用于道德与实际事务。

items.en: Statistics and signal processing gave the old act of sifting a new object: structure hidden in noise.
items.cn: 统计学与信号处理给古老的筛分动作配上新对象：藏在噪声里的结构。

note.en: The first group shares the sifting root or its English descendants; the second group names nearby acts of seeing and distinguishing. Discern is an act of perception that separates something faint from its background, while deduce is a chain of steps from premises to a conclusion.
note.cn: 第一组共享筛分词根或其英语后裔；第二组是相邻的看见与区分动作。本词是从背景中分离出模糊之物的感知动作，推演类词则是从前提走向结论的步骤链。

entries.definition: The capacity for fine judgement, especially about people and values.
entries.definitionCN: 精细判断的能力，尤其关于人与价值。

entries.definition: Showing good judgement, as in a discerning reader.
entries.definitionCN: 显示良好判断力的，如有眼力的读者。

entries.definition: Careful about what one says; it comes from the same Latin participle but lost the seeing.
entries.definitionCN: 说话谨慎；出自同一个拉丁分词，却丢掉了「看见」之义。

entries.definition: Separate and distinct, which is the literal sense of the shared participle.
entries.definitionCN: 分开而独立的，正是那个共享分词的字面义。

entries.definition: To become aware of something through the senses; it is the general word.
entries.definitionCN: 通过感官觉察某物；是泛称。

entries.definition: To mark a difference between things; the emphasis is on the difference, not the faintness.
entries.definitionCN: 标出事物间的差别；强调差别，而非微弱。

entries.definition: To discover something hidden or hard to notice, often by instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 发现隐藏或难以察觉之物，常借助仪器。

entries.definition: To draw fine distinctions; also used for unfair treatment, a sense this word avoids.
entries.definitionCN: 作精细区分；也用于不公平对待，而本词避开后一义。

entries.definition: To manage to see or hear something with difficulty; the everyday phrase for the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 费力地看清或听清；是第一个义项的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the sifting root, the real family and the fixed phrases of perception and judgement.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用筛分词根、真实同族词，以及感知与判断方面的固定搭配。

normal.en: The root means to sift, so the verb means to separate one thing from everything around it.
normal.cn: 词根意为筛分，动词就是把某物从周围一切中分出来。

normal.en: The family runs discernment, discerning, discernible and indiscernible.
normal.cn: 同族词有辨别力、有眼力的、可辨认的与难以辨认的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: discern a difference, discern the truth, barely discern.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：辨出差别、辨明真相、勉强辨认。

normal.en: The eye and the mind share the verb, which is why judgement is described as clear sight.
normal.cn: 眼睛与心智共用这个动词，因此判断被描述成清晰的看见。

normal.en: Two look-alike adjectives came from the same participle: one means tactful, one means separate.
normal.cn: 两个形近形容词出自同一分词：一个表示谨慎，一个表示分离。

abstract.en: Picture a shape slowly separating itself from a grey wall of fog.
abstract.cn: 想象一个形状慢慢从灰色的雾墙中分离出来。

abstract.en: Picture two nearly identical threads that only a careful hand can tell apart.
abstract.cn: 想象两根几乎一样的线，只有细心的手能分开。

abstract.en: Picture a single clear note heard under the noise of a whole street.
abstract.cn: 想象整条街的喧闹下，一个清亮的音符被听见。

examples.en: It was hard to discern anything in the dark room.
examples.cn: 在漆黑的房间里很难看清任何东西。

examples.en: She discerned a note of worry beneath his calm voice.
examples.cn: 她从他平静的声音里辨出一丝担忧。

examples.en: The study discerns no clear trend in the data.
examples.cn: 这项研究在数据中看不出明确的趋势。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迪」加「森」——从雾里把轮廓一丝丝筛出来：辨明、看出

root: 拉丁语「分开」前缀加「筛分」动词构成「分开以看清」，十四世纪经法语进入英语；核心是把微弱之物从背景中筛出来。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all separate a faint thing from its background: an outline, a difference, the truth, a pattern, a motive, right from wrong, a taste and a signal in noise.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把微弱之物从背景中分离出来：轮廓、差别、真相、模式、动机、是非、味道与噪声中的信号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the outline of a lamp slowly emerging from grey fog, after the eye has separated it from the background.
core.cn: 核心意象：雾里一盏灯的轮廓慢慢从灰白中浮出来，眼睛要先分开背景才看得见它。

branches.en: THE SENSES: a dim outline made out, and two similar things told apart.
branches.cn: 感官：看清模糊轮廓，并分辨两个相似之物。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT: the real cause understood, and right separated from wrong.
branches.cn: 判断：理解真正原因，并把是非分开。

branches.en: THE PATTERN: a regularity extracted from a mass of detail.
branches.cn: 模式：从大量细节中抽出的规律。

branches.en: THE PERSON: an intention read beneath what is said.
branches.cn: 人：从言语之下读出的意图。

branches.en: THE FINE DIFFERENCE: a slight taste distinguished, and a weak signal found in noise.
branches.cn: 细微差别：辨出细微味道，以及在噪声中找到微弱信号。

intro.en: Discern is a Latin verb of sifting, and its family supplies the noun for judgement, two adjectives and a pair of look-alike forms that lost the visual sense.

items.example: English kept a shortened form of the Latin verb.

items.example: It builds the noun for the capacity of judgement.

definition_en: to release a substance, a person or a duty, or the substance that is released
core_image: 水管口喷出一股白水，落在石头上溅起一片雾
scene: 工厂的管子对着河面，水色发灰，岸边浮着一层沫。The factory was fined for discharging waste into the river.
sceneCN: 这里 discharging 指「排放」（第 1 个义项：把液体或气体排出）；句意是这家工厂因向河里排放废物被罚款。

senses.title: To let a substance flow out
senses.definition: to release liquid, gas or waste into the environment
senses.definitionCN: 把液体、气体或废物排到环境里
senses.example: The factory was fined for discharging waste into the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂因向河里排放废物被罚款。
senses.why: The pipe does not ask the river whether it wants the water.
senses.whyCN: 管子不问河水要不要这些水，只管往外放。

senses.title: To allow someone to leave
senses.definition: to allow a patient, soldier or prisoner to leave officially
senses.definitionCN: 正式允许病人、军人或囚犯离开
senses.example: She was discharged from hospital on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 她周五出院了。
senses.why: The door opens only when someone with authority says it may.
senses.whyCN: 那扇门，只有在有权的人说可以时才会开。

senses.title: To carry out a duty or pay a debt
senses.definition: to perform a duty fully or to pay what is owed
senses.definitionCN: 把职责做到底，或把欠的还清
senses.example: He discharged his duties without complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 他毫无怨言地履行了职责。
senses.why: A load is set down only when nothing is left on it.
senses.whyCN: 只有什么都不剩了，肩上的担子才算卸下。

intro.en: Discharge came from Old French deschargier, to unload, built on chargier, to load, and Latin carrus, a cart.
intro.cn: discharge 来自古法语 deschargier（卸货），词基 chargier 意为装载，更早是拉丁语 carrus（车）。

items.en: Carrus named a four-wheeled cart.
items.cn: carrus 指四轮货车。

items.en: Carricare meant to load a cart or a beast.
items.cn: carricare 指往车上或牲口背上装货。

items.en: Chargier meant to load, and deschargier meant to unload.
items.cn: chargier 指装载，deschargier 指卸下。

items.en: Discharge first meant to unload goods or a ship.
items.cn: discharge 最初指卸货或卸船。

items.en: The word widened to waste, patients, soldiers and duties.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到废物、病人、军人与职责。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the charge stem, while the meaning group names other kinds of letting go.
note.cn: 形近组共用 charge 这一段词干，近义组则列出其他放手的说法。

entries.definition: to load, to ask a price, or to accuse
entries.definitionCN: 装载、收费或指控

entries.definition: a device that puts power into a battery
entries.definitionCN: 给电池充电的装置

entries.definition: to put fresh power into a battery
entries.definitionCN: 给电池重新充电

entries.definition: to let a person or substance go free
entries.definitionCN: 让人或物质自由离开

entries.definition: to send out light, sound or gas
entries.definitionCN: 发出光、声音或气体

entries.definition: to send someone away or remove them from a job
entries.definitionCN: 让某人离开，或解除其职务

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a pipe pouring into a river to a duty finally paid in full.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从往河里灌水的管子，走到终于还清的职责。

normal.en: Dis- plus charge: the load is taken off.
normal.cn: dis- 加 charge：把担子卸下来。

normal.en: A pipe discharges; a ward discharges; a soldier is discharged.
normal.cn: 管子排放，病房放人，军人退役，都是这个词。

normal.en: To discharge a duty is to leave nothing owed.
normal.cn: 履行职责，就是把欠的都清掉。

normal.en: The river carries away what the pipe lets go.
normal.cn: 管子放出的东西，由河水带走。

normal.en: The word always means a load leaving a place.
normal.cn: 这个词始终意味着：有一份重量离开了原处。

abstract.en: Picture grey water spreading under a pipe.
abstract.cn: 想象灰水在管口下面散开。

abstract.en: Picture a hospital door opening for a walking patient.
abstract.cn: 想象病房的门为一个能走路的病人打开。

abstract.en: Picture an empty cart with its wheels still turning.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆空车，轮子还在转。

examples.en: The factory was fined for discharging waste into the river.
examples.cn: 这家工厂因向河里排放废物被罚款。

examples.en: She was discharged from hospital on Friday.
examples.cn: 她周五出院了。

examples.en: He discharged his duties without complaint.
examples.cn: 他毫无怨言地履行了职责。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discharge 记成「的士查值」：的士到站查完值就卸客，人货一起放出去。

root: 来自古法语 deschargier（卸货），由表示「去除」的 des- 加 chargier（装载）构成，更早可追到拉丁语 carrus（车）。本义是把货从车上卸下，后来引申为排出液体与气体、准许病人或军人离开，以及履行完职责、还清债务，仿佛卸下肩上的重担。

sensesIntro.en: From waste leaving a pipe, to a patient leaving a ward, to a duty leaving a person's shoulders.
sensesIntro.cn: 从离开管口的废物，到离开病房的病人，再到离开肩头的职责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pipe pouring out, and a cart standing empty.
core.cn: 核心意象：管子往外倒，车子空了下来。

branches.en: The first sense is a substance let out.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是被放出来的物质。

branches.en: The second sense is a person allowed to go.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是被准许离开的人。

branches.en: The third sense is a load of duty carried to the end.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是扛到底、终于卸下的职责。

branches.en: Water and people both leave through an opening.
branches.cn: 水与人，都是从某个出口离开。

branches.en: Leaving a post and finishing a duty are two ends of one service.

latinIntro.en: Latin carrus, a cart, gives carricare, to load, and through French the base charge.

items.exampleCN: 出租车司机想多收我们的钱。

items.meaning: loaded with power or filled with feeling

definition_zh: n. 门徒；弟子；信徒；（学说、流派的）追随者
definition_en: a person who follows a teacher or believes in and spreads the ideas of a leader or school
core_image: 画室里两副并排的画架，老师改过的画稿压在学生那张下面；墙上师生作品挂在一起
scene: 他是那位画家的关门弟子。He was the last disciple of the painter.
sceneCN: 这里 disciple 是「亲授弟子」（第 1 个义项：跟随某位老师学习并传承其技艺）；句意是他是那位画家的最后一位弟子。图中可辨识物件：画室里两副画架、老师改过的画稿、墙上并排挂着的师生作品。

senses.title: A taught follower

senses.definitionCN: （名词）直接向师父学习并传承其教导的人
senses.example: He was the last disciple of the painter.
senses.exampleCN: 他是那位画家的最后一位弟子。
senses.why: Two easels side by side with the master corrections under the student sheet.
senses.whyCN: 两副并排的画架，老师的批改压在学生那张下面。

senses.title: A religious believer
senses.definition: a follower of a religious leader, especially in early Christianity
senses.definitionCN: （名词）宗教领袖的追随者，尤指早期基督教
senses.example: The twelve disciples travelled with their teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 十二门徒与他们的老师同行。
senses.why: A dusty road with a group walking behind one figure.
senses.whyCN: 一条尘土路上，一群人跟在一个身影后面。

senses.title: An adherent of a school

items.en: Discipulus named a pupil.
items.cn: discipulus 指学生。

items.en: Disciplina named teaching and training.
items.cn: disciplina 指教养与训练。

items.en: Old English borrowed it for a follower.
items.cn: 古英语借入后指追随者。

items.en: It named the followers of Jesus in English gospels.

items.en: It now names followers of any thinker.

definition_en: training that produces obedience and control, a field of study, or punishment
core_image: 操场上鞋跟并拢的响声，一排人影在晨光里排成直线
scene: 天还没亮，哨声一响，所有人从床上弹起，几十秒后站成四列。Good discipline kept the team calm under pressure.
sceneCN: 这里 discipline 指「纪律」（第 1 个义项：让人守规矩的约束）；句意是良好的纪律让团队在压力下保持冷静。

senses.title: Training that makes people obey
senses.definition: training and rules that produce order and self-control
senses.definitionCN: 带来秩序与自制的训练和规则
senses.example: Good discipline kept the team calm under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的纪律让团队在压力下保持冷静。
senses.why: A line of people moves as one only when each one holds still.
senses.whyCN: 一排人只有各自站住，才能像一个整体那样动。

senses.title: A field of study

senses.definitionCN: 在学校或研究中钻研的一个知识分支

senses.exampleCN: 她同时学两门学科。
senses.why: A mind in training is organised like a body in training.
senses.whyCN: 受训的心，和受训的身体一样有条理。

senses.title: To punish and correct
senses.definition: to train someone by punishment or firm control
senses.definitionCN: 用惩罚或严格管束来训练某人
senses.example: The teacher disciplined the class firmly.
senses.exampleCN: 老师严格管教了这个班。
senses.why: The word turns from the rule into the hand that enforces it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从规矩本身，转成执行规矩的那只手。

intro.en: Discipline comes from Latin disciplina, instruction, from discere, to learn, and discipulus, a learner.
intro.cn: discipline 来自拉丁语 disciplina（教导），词根 discere 意为学习，discipulus 指学习者。

items.en: Discere meant to learn, and discipulus meant a learner.
items.cn: discere 指学习，discipulus 指学习者。

items.cn: disciplina 指教导、知识以及有秩序的行为。

items.en: Discipline carried the sense of instruction and correction.
items.cn: 这个词在古法语里兼指教导与纠正。

items.en: English discipline meant training, especially of the mind.
items.cn: 英语里的 discipline 指训练，尤指心智的训练。

items.en: It widened to a field of study and to punishment.

entries.definition: able to control one's own behaviour

entries.definition: a state in which everything is in its right place

entries.definition: a penalty given for a wrong act

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a whistle at dawn to a subject that trains the mind.

normal.en: Discipline and disciple share a root: both are about learning.
normal.cn: discipline 与 disciple 同根，都和学习有关。

normal.en: A line of shoes on a field is discipline you can see.
normal.cn: 操场上排齐的鞋，是看得见的纪律。

normal.cn: 自律是一声不需要别人吹的哨。

normal.en: A discipline is also a subject, trained like a muscle.
normal.cn: 学科也是一门功夫，要像肌肉一样练。

normal.en: To discipline a child is to teach, not only to punish.
normal.cn: 管教孩子是为了教，不只是为了罚。

abstract.cn: 想象四排影子一动不动地站着。

abstract.cn: 想象一声哨响划过清冷的晨空。

examples.en: Good discipline kept the team calm under pressure.

examples.en: The teacher disciplined the class firmly.

sensesIntro.en: From a body trained to stand in line, to a mind trained in one field, to the hand that corrects.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被训练得站成一条线的身体，到在一个领域受训的心，再到那只纠正人的手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of people standing still at the sound of a whistle.
core.cn: 核心意象：哨声一响，一排排人静静站定。

branches.en: The first sense is the order that training produces.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是训练带来的秩序。

branches.en: The second sense is the field a trained mind works in.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是受训的心所钻研的领域。

branches.en: The third sense is the correction that keeps the order.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是维持秩序的纠正。

branches.en: A trained body and a trained mind follow the same habit.
branches.cn: 受训的身体和心智，遵循同一种习惯。

branches.en: Without correction, the line slowly bends.
branches.cn: 没有纠正，那条线就会慢慢弯掉。

intro.en: Discipline gathers the discip- family, words about learning, order and correction.
intro.cn: discipline 聚起 discip 一族词，围绕学习、秩序与纠正。

latinIntro.en: Latin discere, to learn, gives discipulus, a learner, and disciplina, teaching.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 discere（学习）给出 discipulus（学习者）与 disciplina（教导）。

items.example: The school is known for its discipline.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校以纪律严明著称。

items.meaning: a learner who follows a teacher
items.example: He was a disciple of the old master.
items.exampleCN: 他是那位老大师的弟子。

items.example: She is a disciplined worker.
The company began a disciplinary hearing.

items.meaning: a person who enforces strict rules
items.example: The coach was a firm disciplinarian.
items.exampleCN: 这位教练纪律要求很严。

items.meaning: the act of training or correcting
items.example: Disciplining a child takes patience.

items.meaning: fields of study or sets of rules
items.example: The library serves many disciplines.
items.exampleCN: 这座图书馆服务许多学科。

items.example: The undisciplined crowd pushed forward.
items.exampleCN: 没有秩序的人群往前挤。
